prerequisites: Successful completion of modules from the 1st and 2nd semesters as per study plan

learning_outcomes.text: Students know the essential fundamentals and approaches in lightweight construction and can classify and describe lightweight-appropriate materials.
Students can reproduce application-oriented basic knowledge about relevant lightweight materials and name, compare, and categorize their alloy structure, heat treatment, and forming possibilities.
Students can assess the material behavior of components and constructions, including after welding operations.
Students are able to apply the principles of lightweight construction to specific problems.
Students can assess the application possibilities and potentials of metallic lightweight materials.
Students recognize and consider that consistent lightweight construction is only possible when, in addition to the material consideration, all relevant areas such as design are viewed holistically.

syllabus_topics: Introduction and fundamentals of lightweight materials
Aspects, methods, and strategies of material selection
Properties of basic materials Al, Mg, Ti
Application examples and aspects of using aluminum based on one or more current development projects
Further lightweight materials such as plastics and fiber-reinforced composites (FRP), technical ceramics
Fundamentals, properties, processing, application of plastics, FRP, and technical ceramics
assessment_rules: The final module examination (Modulabschlussprüfung) can be a written exam lasting 180-240 minutes or an oral exam lasting 45-60 minutes. The allocation of credit points is granted upon passing the module final examination. In the exam, students should explain elementary processes for exemplary problems, select suitable solutions and materials, and evaluate them regarding their properties.
